rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom begins in causality and creation; divine wisdom creates effects in an ordered chain of beneficial causes and results, called God’s established way.
rows.anchor: Hikmet, nisbet-i illiyete râci‘, illiyetin hakikati de halk u îcad olduğundan asıl hikmet îcad demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human wisdom makes works that benefit others and become causes for further benefits, while humans remain instruments of God’s creation rather than its first cause.
rows.anchor: İnsanların hikmeti de diğer ibâdullahın menâfi‘ve mesâlihi bulunan şeyler yapması, sünnet-i ilâhiyeyi fehm ve ona göre bir îcâd u ihtirâ‘a sebep olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition makes wisdom putting every thing in its proper place and rank; it can describe both comprehensive divine wisdom and particular human wisdom.
rows.anchor: Hikmet: Eşyâyı mevzi ve mertebesine koymak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom entails ordered creation; creating without order falls outside its meaning, and this definition is especially well known as a definition of justice.
rows.anchor: bilâ tertîb îcad, mefhûm-ı hikmetten hâriç olur. Ma‘amâfîh bu târif, vaz‘-ı sânî mülâhazasıyla daha ziyade “adl”in târifi olmak üzere meşhurdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related definition equates wisdom with justice, the ethical foundation between excess and deficiency.
rows.anchor: hikmet, adalet demek olur. Hikmet-i ameliye denilen nazarî ilm-i ahlâkı ifrat ve tefrit beyninde adl esası üzerine binâ edenler bu mânayı almışlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is also defined as persistently undertaking sound, good deeds; this makes it a stable moral disposition directed toward good.
rows.anchor: Ef‘âl-i hasene-i sâibeye ikdamdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acting with a praiseworthy outcome is offered as a closely related definition of wisdom.
rows.anchor: Âkıbeti mahmud olan fiili yapmak” târifi de buna karîbdir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: In governance, wisdom means following the Creator as far as human capacity allows, by affirming His knowledge, just action, generosity, and forbearance.
rows.anchor: ilmini cehilden, fiilini cevrden, cûdunu buhlden, hilmini sefehden tenzih ile olur (Fahreddin Râzî tefsirinden)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that each person is a shepherd shows that this governance-oriented definition applies generally, not only to political rulers.
rows.anchor: bu târif her hâlde hikmetin hâkimiyet mânasıyla alâkasını ibraz eyler.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi defines wisdom as acquiring divine moral qualities; a hadith likewise urges people to take on God’s qualities.
rows.anchor: Hikmet: Ahlâk-ı ilâhiye ile tahalluk[^52](Râzî)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s great character is the foremost example of divine and Qur’anic morality, and completing noble character is presented as the purpose of his mission.
rows.anchor: âyet-i celîlesi de bunun en büyük misâlini göstermiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason, understanding, faith, gnosis, and knowledge are prerequisites for embodying divine character, while reflection belongs to the wise.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki akıl, fehm, iman, marifet, ilim bu tahallukun erkânından değilse şerâitindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True wisdom joins sound knowledge with sound action: knowledge should cause beneficial action, and action should derive from knowledge.
rows.anchor: Yani hikmet ya ilm-i savâb veya fi‘l-i savâb değil, ilm-i savâb ile fi‘l-i savâbdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither theoretical knowledge by itself nor accidental action uninformed by knowledge is wisdom; divine wisdom contains neither.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir ilm-i nazarî bizzat bir hikmet olmadığı gibi, tesadüfî olan herhangi bir amel-i gayr-i ilmî de öyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causality rules out chance as an account of reality; what people call chance reflects ignorance of causes, and treating nature as the first cause is unscientific.
rows.anchor: Tesadüf, hakikate ve ilme nazaran değil, sebebini bilmeyen cehle nazarandır. Tesadüf nazariyesi dâima cehil nazariyesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every being relates to God directly, grounding its distinct existence and faith in divine power, and through an endless mediated chain of causes, which reason and science can study.
rows.anchor: bizzat bir istinad ve müsebbebiyettir ki her şeyin hususiyeti bununla kāimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect humans recognize their authority as a current of divine sovereignty rather than claiming independent primacy; Abraham attributed life and death to God, while Nimrod claimed the power himself.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i İbrâhim sırr-ı ihyâya nâil olduğu hâlde اَنَا اُحْـيِ وَاُميتُ demeyip رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ [el-Bakara 2/258] demiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason, heart, and soul are gifts from God; human acts arise through acquisition yet remain divine gifts both directly and through means.
rows.anchor: akıl, sırf bir ‘atıyye-i[^60] ilâhiye olduğu gibi, mebde’-i izzet olan kalb ve nefs de bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants wisdom to distinguish truth from falsehood and divine from satanic promises, then to act rightly and prevent harm while bringing benefit.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah dilediğine hak ile bâtılı, va‘d-i ilâhî ile va‘d-i şeytânîyi fehm ü temyiz ederek ona göre amel-i savâbı yapacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge and understanding are necessary conditions, not sufficient causes, for perfected action; reflection and use of the will are also required, with each person receiving wisdom according to intellect.
rows.anchor: Fakat ilim ve fehm amel-i muhkem için bir sebep veya şart olmakla beraber illet-i tâmme olmayacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection gradually becomes a God-given disposition, strengthening practical reason so a person reliably follows what is true and sound in knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: Bilâhare bu tezekkür ve o hikmet feyz-i Hak ile bir meleke olur da insan mertebesine göre ahlâk-ı ilâhiye ile tahalluk eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theoretical learning alone becomes wordplay and can mislead; beneficial knowledge must lead to action, while stressing knowledge warns that action without knowledge is not wisdom.
rows.anchor: Lâkin yalnız bunda tevakkuf edip kalmak, şeytana yol kestirmek demektir, bu nihâyet bir feylesofluktur. Yani hikmet değil, hikmet lafı etmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reconciles definitions centered on action and knowledge: each is a component of wisdom, whose complete form is sound knowledge together with sound action.
rows.anchor: Demek ki asıl hakikat ikisinin ictimâ‘ındadır. O hâlde evvelki târifleri esas olarak almak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theoretical reflection is a prelude to practical wisdom and should carry the person from knowing God to worship, fulfilling the purpose of creation.
rows.anchor: her hâlde mârifetten ubûdiyete geçilip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is a book of wisdom and the Qur’an recalls its inner meanings; one must observe the present order, remember its beginning and end, obey it, and seek afterlife happiness.
rows.anchor: Âlem bir kitâb-ı hikmettir. Kur’an da bu hikmetin ledünniyâtını tezkir ve ihtar eder. Âlem bir hâl, Kur’an da bu hâlin evvel ü âhiridir.

rows.speaker: İbn Kāsım
rows.claim: Ibn Qasim, as cited by Qushayri, defines wisdom as reflection on God’s command and following Him.
rows.anchor: Hikmet: Tefekkür fî emrillah ve O’na ittibâ‘dır (İbn Kāsım’dan Kuşeyrî).

rows.speaker: Kuşeyrî
rows.claim: Qushayri also defines wisdom as obedience to God, jurisprudence, religion, and action.
rows.anchor: Hikmet: Allah’a tâat, fıkıh, din, ameldir (Kuşeyrî).

rows.speaker: Ebu Osman
rows.claim: Abu Uthman calls wisdom a light that distinguishes divine inspiration from whispering.
rows.anchor: Hikmet bir nûrdur ki vesvese ile makam beyni bununla fark edilir (Ebu Osman)

rows.speaker: Bündar İbnü’l-Hüseyn
rows.claim: Bundar ibn al-Husayn defines wisdom as a swift answer accompanied by correctness.
rows.anchor: Sür‘at-i cevab ma‘a isâbeti’s-savâb (Bündar İbnü’l-Hüseyn)

rows.speaker: Mufaddal
rows.claim: Mufaddal defines wisdom as returning to what is correct.
rows.anchor: 16. Savâba red (Mufaddal

rows.speaker: Kettânî
rows.claim: Kettani defines wisdom as spirits reaching their utmost calm and serenity.
rows.anchor: Ervâhın müntehâ-yı sükûnet ve itmi’nânı (Kettânî)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition is an unqualified sign from God, beyond whom no cause can be imagined, leaving no doubt or need to ask why.
rows.anchor: yani mâfevkinde illet tasavvur olunmayan Hak teâlâ’dan bilâ kayd ü şart vârid olup şekk ü şüphe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is also described as witnessing the Real in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: Cemî‘ahvâle hakkı işhâd.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition is the soundness of religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: Salâh-ı dîn ü dünya.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is identified with knowledge received from God’s presence.
rows.anchor: İlm-i ledünnî.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom can mean inward purification so the heart is ready to receive inspiration.
rows.anchor: Vürûd-i ilham için tecrîd-i sır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says some definitions ground wisdom in the heart and conscience, the meeting point of knowledge, reason, and will.
rows.anchor: bunların bazıları hikmet ilm ü amel derken meseleyi kalb ve vicdâna dayamışlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conscience is the self immediately finding itself; the heart is this center of unity, with spiritual life formed by alternating activity and receptivity.
rows.anchor: Kalb dediğimiz şey de nefsin bu merkez-i vahdetidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual contraction and expansion receive support from divine breath, and their transitions are experienced as pain and pleasure; life depends on the heart’s alternating turns.
rows.anchor: Enfâs-ı rahmâniyenin çekilmesi bir inkıbaz, vürûdu da bir inbisat ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A life of wisdom requires balance: prolonged contraction or expansion becomes illness, while health rests in alternating pain and pleasure and balanced fear and hope.
rows.anchor: istikbale nazaran hikmet, ye’s ü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word wisdom can denote sound knowledge, praiseworthy character, useful craft or benefit, causality, prevention of harm, admonition, mysteries, prophecy, established custom, Sunnah, law, religion, scripture, Qur’an, or Gospel.
rows.anchor: ma‘lûmât-ı muhkeme, ahlâk-ı hamîde, sınâ‘at-ı nâfi‘a, menfa‘at-i müterettibe ve maksûde

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil gives Qur’anic exhortations as one sense of wisdom, exemplified by 2:231.
rows.anchor: Mevâ‘iz-i Kur’an mânasına hikmet ki Sûre-i Bakara’da وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَٱلْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦ

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil gives understanding and knowledge as another sense of wisdom, exemplified by 31:12.
rows.anchor: Fehm ü ilim mânasına hikmet ki وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا لُقْمَٰنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil gives prophethood as a sense of wisdom, exemplified in the references to Abraham’s family and Solomon.
rows.anchor: Nübüvvet mânasına hikmet ki Sûre-i Nisâ’da فَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ ءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil also takes wisdom to mean the Qur’an with its marvelous mysteries, citing 16:125 and this verse.
rows.anchor: Acâib-i esrârıyla Kur’an ki Sûre-i Nahl’de ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says the four senses ultimately reduce to knowledge.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî de bu dört mânanın ‘inde’t-tahkīk ilim mânasına râci‘olduğunu

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd ve Dahhâk
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Dahhak, and others explain wisdom as the Qur’an itself.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd ve Dahhâk vesâireden يُؤْتِى ٱلْحِكْمَةَ مَن يَشَآءُ’da “hikmetten murad Kur’an’dır” diye

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas defines wisdom as knowing the Qur’an’s abrogating and abrogated, decisive and ambiguous, earlier and later passages.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’dan bir rivayette, “Kur’ân’ın nâsih ve mensûhunu, muhkem ve müteşabihini, mukaddem ve muahharını mârifettir” diye

rows.speaker: İbrâhim, Ebü’l-Âliye ve Katâde
rows.claim: Ibrahim, Abu al-Aliya, and Qatada explain wisdom as understanding the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim ve Ebü’l-Âliye ve Katâde’den “fehm-i Kur’an” diye

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan interprets wisdom as wary reverence in God’s religion.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan “vera‘fî dînillah” diye

rows.speaker: Rebî‘b. Enes
rows.claim: Rabi ibn Anas interprets wisdom as fear of God.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes’den “haşyet” diye tefsir edildiği de menkuldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many interpretations reduce to knowledge that leads to beneficial action, beneficial action derived from knowledge, or thoroughness and correctness in both; they are closely related and need not be restricted.
rows.anchor: bu tafsîlât kısmen misâl ve târife haml edilmek suretiyle mecmû‘u üç tefsîre ircâ‘olunabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the definite article and promise of abundant good may suggest the wisdom of prophecy or the Qur’an, context and mention of acquisition favor the general essence of wisdom.
rows.anchor: muhakkikīnin muhtarları bu üç mânadan ma‘nâ-yı masdarî veya hâsıl-ı masdar olarak bilâ tahsis tefsirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every kind of wisdom is God’s gift, but abundant good belongs to complete wisdom, and the most perfect wisdom is universal good.
rows.anchor: Her nevi hikmet Allah’ın ihsânıdır. Fakat hayr-ı kesîr hikmet-i kâmilededir. Ekmel hikmet de hayr-ı küldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only learned practitioners and people of wisdom reflect on God’s reminders and distinguish His promise from Satan’s; others may succumb to Satan because their hearts and minds are unsound.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın bu tezkîrâtını ulü’l-elbâb olan âlim-i âmil erbâb-ı hikmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every expenditure and vow, whether small or large, pure or corrupt, spent for God or Satan, and whether made in obedience or sin; He rewards or punishes accordingly.
rows.anchor: az veya çok, habis veya tayyib, gerek Allah yolunda ve gerek şeytan yolunda her ne niyetle her ne nafaka sarf ü infak eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must not disguise sin as obedience, withhold God’s or others’ rights, or wrong themselves by concealing or changing what is due.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan bir şey gizlenir zannedip de masiyeti tâat, tâati masiyet yerine koymamalı; hukūkullâhı, hukūk-ı ‘ibâdı men‘ü tağyir ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Injustice includes diverting charity to sins, changing vows of obedience into sinful acts, withholding obligatory charity or vows, giving corrupt goods, giving for show or with reminders, and otherwise altering people’s or God’s rights; wrongdoers ultimately harm themselves and find no helper.
rows.anchor: Zulüm herhangi bir şeyi hakkı ve lâyıkı olan mevzi‘inin gayrısına koymak demek olduğundan, hayır tohumu ekmek için yapılması lâzım gelen infakları me‘âsî ve şurûra sarf ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge ensures that wrongdoers receive their fitting punishment; the passage alludes to the principle that fear of God is the root of wisdom.
rows.anchor: İlm-i ilâhî onların hiçbir niyetini, hiçbir hareketini kaçırmayacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking benefit depends on love of God, while preventing harm depends on reverent fear; genuine love includes awe, obedience, and concern not to displease the beloved.
rows.anchor: Hikmetin celb-i maslahat mânası, mahabbetullâha mütevakkıf olduğu gibi ona mütekaddim olan def‘-i mefsedet mânası da mehâfetullâha müterettibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As love rises, reverent fear rises too; those nearest to God fear that acts praised in ordinary people could count as sins for the especially close, and the verse warns in three stages from reflection to judgment.
rows.anchor: İşte Cenâb-ı Allah beyân-ı hikmetten sonra bu merâtib-i mehâfete işâreten evvelâ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the verse about spending was revealed, people asked the Prophet whether charity is better given secretly or openly, and the answer came in this verse.
rows.anchor: işbu وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُم مِّن نَّفَقَةٍ âyeti nâzil olduğu zaman Resûlullah’a “sadakanın gizlisi mi efdal, âşikâresi mi?” diye sormuşlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Open charity is good when free of ostentation; giving secretly to the poor is better and can become a means for God to cover some sins.
rows.anchor: Eğer sadakaları açıktan, alenen verirseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiraat differ on the verb for covering sins: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Shu‘ba from Asim, and Yaqub read with nūn; Nafi, Hamza, Kisai, Abu Ja‘far, and Khalaf read with nūn and a jussive rā’.
rows.anchor: وَيُكَفِّرُ, İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir Şu‘be, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde نون ile نُكَفِّرُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sadaqah may refer to obligatory or voluntary charity, while zakat refers only to obligatory charity.
rows.anchor: “Sadaka”, farza da nâfileye de ıtlak olunur. خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ صَدَقَةًۭ تُطَهِّرُهُمْ

rows.speaker: Ehl-i lügat
rows.claim: Lexicographers derive sadaqah from a root meaning soundness and completeness; mahr is called sadaq because marriage is completed by it.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i lügat demişlerdir ki “sadaka”nın aslı olan ص د ق maddesi bu tertip üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Charity is called sadaqah because it purifies and perfects wealth and indicates sincerity and completeness in faith.
rows.anchor: Zekâta “sadaka” ıtlak edilmesi de iki vechiledir. Birisi malın tahâretiyle sıhhat ü kemâline sebep olması, diğeri de imanda sıdk u kemâle delâlet etmesidir.

rows.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most commentators treat the definite article in “the charities” as referring to voluntary alms, since obligatory charity is better shown publicly.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirîn ‘ahd için olup yalnız sadakāt-ı nâfileye masruf olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators instead restrict the definite article to obligatory charity and read “better for you” as simply “a good thing.”
rows.anchor: bazısı ‘ahd için olmakla beraber yalnız farza mahmul olduğuna kāil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî ve muhakkikīn
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri and other verifying scholars take the article inclusively, covering obligatory and voluntary charity; the author prefers this view.
rows.anchor: başta Hasan-ı Basrî hazretleri olmak üzere diğer bir kısım müfessirîn lâm-ı istiğrak olarak farz u nâfileden e‘am olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır ki muhakkikīnin muhtârı da budur.

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu al-Suud and others see a balanced division: the first clause commends public giving of obligatory charity, the second prefers secrecy for voluntary charity.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud ve sâirenin beyânına göre âyette bu mâna üzere güzel bir üslûb-ı taksim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For wealth that can be concealed, such as cash, zakat is best given openly absent a risk; when public giving would cause harm or misdirect it, secrecy is better, while crops and livestock are observable.
rows.anchor: mahzur bulunduğu ve meselâ açıktan verildiği zaman mahall-i lâyıkına teslim olunamayacağı takdirde bunu da nâfile gibi gizli vermek efdal olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says voluntary charity is seventy times better in secret, while obligatory charity is seventy times better in public; the verse’s division points to this distinction.
rows.anchor: tetavvu‘da sırren vermek alenen vermekten yetmiş kat efdal, farzda da alenen vermek gizli vermekten yetmiş kat efdal olduğu beyan olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all that people do openly or secretly, so advertising charity to inform God is pointless and secrecy is more sincere.
rows.anchor: habîrdir. Binâen‘aleyh Allah’a bildirmek için sadakalarınızı dünyaya ilan etmeye kalkışmakta da mâna yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret voluntary charity avoids ostentation, reputation-seeking, and reminding recipients; the Prophet says God accepts nothing from one who seeks notice, shows off, or reminds others of favors.
rows.anchor: Allah ne işittiren süm‘acıdan, ne gösteriş yapan mürâîden, ne de minnetçiden bir şey kabul etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exemplary Muslims hid their giving even from recipients to avoid showing off, seeking praise, or creating a sense of indebtedness.
rows.anchor: sadakalarını verecekleri fakire bile bildirmemeye çalışan birçok zevât geçmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secrecy denies the ego public fame and praise, making the deed harder and its reward greater.
rows.anchor: beyne’n-nâs şöhret, medh ü ta‘zîm husûle gelmez, bu da nefse zor gelir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best charity is the effort of someone with little who gives secretly to a poor person.
rows.anchor: Sadakanın efdali az bir şeyi olanın fakire gizli olarak verdiği cühdü, yani gücünün son yettiğidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says a secret deed is recorded as secret, then as public if disclosed, and as ostentation if the giver talks about it.
rows.anchor: Kul sırren bir amel yapar Allah da onu sırren yazar, sonra bu ameli izhar ederse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known hadith includes among the seven sheltered on Judgment Day a giver whose left hand does not know what the right hand gave.
rows.anchor: bir sadaka verip sağ elinin verdiğini sol eli bilmeyen adamdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hadith says secret charity extinguishes the Lord’s anger.
rows.anchor: Sadaka-i sır gazab-ı Rabbi söndürür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public giving can violate the recipient’s dignity by exposing poverty, undermine the self-restraint praised in the next verse, or invite suspicion and gossip about whether the recipient deserves help.
rows.anchor: İzharda fakirin nâmus ve haysiyetine dokunmak, fakrını ilan etmek vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public charity can humiliate a recipient because the giver’s upper hand is better than the receiver’s lower hand; giving resembles a gift, and witnesses may be treated as sharing it.
rows.anchor: yed-i ‘ulyâ yed-i süflâdan hayırlı olmak itibariyle izharda fakiri bir tezlil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, rational and transmitted reasons make concealing voluntary charity preferable.
rows.anchor: İşte bütün bu esbâb-ı ma‘kūle ve menkūle nâfile sadakanın ihfâsı efdal olduğuna delâlet ederler

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the Prophet’s distinction: secrecy is generally better, but public giving is better for one who intends others to follow.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer radıyallahu ‘anh’dan rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki “اَلسِّرُّ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ الْعَلَاَنِيَةِ وَالْعَلَاَنِيَةُ أَفْضَلُ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ الْإِْقْتِدَاءَ بِهِ

rows.speaker: Hakîm Tirmizî Muhammed b. Îsâ
rows.claim: Hakim Tirmidhi says that for a person still struggling against the desire to be seen, resisting that desire in a hidden deed is spiritual combat and earns greatly multiplied reward.
rows.anchor: İnsan halktan gizleyerek bir amel yapar ve nefsinde onu halkın görmesini ister bir şehvet bulunduğu hâlde bu şehveti def‘eder durursa

rows.speaker: Hakîm Tirmizî Muhammed b. Îsâ
rows.claim: The spiritually purified can act openly without egoistic motives, solely hoping others will follow and gain reward; exemplary leadership can complete the servant and guide others.
rows.anchor: Bu kendi tekemmül etmiş de başkalarını kemâle erdirmeye sa‘y eden ve bu suretle tam ve hatta fevka’t-tamâm olmak isteyen bir kuldur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture praises people who guide others: the righteous ask to lead the pious, and communities among Moses’ and Muhammad’s followers are praised for guiding with truth and justice.
rows.anchor: Ümmet-i Mûsâ’yı medh ederken وَمِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰٓ أُمَّةٌۭ يَهْدُونَ بِٱلْحَقِّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligatory zakat is better given openly because scripture commands its collection, secrecy risks suspicion, and public delivery signals prompt compliance; hence obligations are public and voluntary gifts private.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ, bu babda خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ صَدَقَةًۭ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is restricted to Muslims because it is a defined debt owed to them, rather than a merely generous gift.
rows.anchor: Zekât yalnız mü’minlere verilir, çünkü o mücerred ihsan değil, hakkı mâlum olan bir borçtur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives reported occasions for the next verse: Asma’s polytheist mother and grandmother sought aid; some Ansar withheld charity from Jewish relatives; and the Prophet reportedly barred aid to polytheists when Muslim poor were numerous, hoping need would lead them to Islam.
rows.anchor: Bu sebeplerden biri veya hepsi dolayısıyla şu âyet nâzil olmuştur

none: The segment contains only Turkish verse renderings and a bare transition, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance of the heavens and earth belongs solely to God: human heirs possess only temporary, borrowed holdings that perish, while God’s ownership remains.
rows.anchor: Semâvât ve arzın mîrâsı, yani seleften halefe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hoard wealth and refuse to spend in God’s path should remember that they are withholding what belongs to its true owner and committing a grave sin.
rows.anchor: Bunlara tevârüs edenlerin milk-i hakīkīleri yoktur; o muvakkat, müste‘âr bir şeydir. Hepsi fâni olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavenly inheritance also includes lofty gifts such as prophethood and knowledge; the verse prepares for the inheritance laws in the following Surah al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: Semâvî miras; nübüvvet, ilim gibi me‘âlîdir. Bundan şu anlaşılır ki evvelâ miras bir kānûn-ı ilâhîdir.
